messages:
From: Mike Tan <mike.tan@acme.health>

Cc: Acme Health DPO <dpo@acme.health>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Locality SLA exceptions and subprocessor roster — pilot questions

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week. We're getting our security team involved as we scope the pilot; they have a few follow-ups before we can sign the statement of work. High level: Acme needs confirmation about where customer data will be stored and which subprocessors will process telemetry and logs. Specific asks below — can you confirm by end of week?

1) For pilot traffic from our APAC customers, can you confirm whether any analytics or aggregated logs will leave APAC at any time (including transient syncs)? If so, what are the maximum sync windows and how often?

2) We need a roster of all subprocessors that could see request payloads or token-level logs for the pilot — including their region and whether they are covered by Redwood's DPA/standard contractual clauses.

3) For keys: where are customer-managed KMS keys stored/created for Private deployments? If using Redwood-managed KMS in hosted mode, can you list key regions and explain transient access by operations?

4) Finally, Acme's legal has asked about carve-outs from the locality SLA for short-lived operational syncs (e.g., debugging, failover). Do you have a proposed policy or a standard process for approving exceptions? If so, please attach.

I've attached our DPA questionnaire. Happy to set a quick call if easier.

Thanks,
Mike
Mike Tan
Head of Security Programs
Acme Health

Attachments: Acme_DPA_Questions.docx
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mike Tan <mike.tan@acme.health>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Locality SLA exceptions and subprocessor roster — pilot questions

Hi Mike — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Grace (privacy lead) and Ben (solutions) to help. Quick answers and next steps below; see attached outline for our operational carve-out policy.

1) Transient syncs: For hosted and dedicated customers, application request payloads and inference KV cache are routed to the selected region by default. We do run background analytics and aggregated telemetry pipelines that may traverse regions for indexing and long-term storage, but for pilot bindings we can enforce a bounded-sync window: up to 24 hours for non-sensitive aggregated metrics, and up to 2 hours for operational debug traces (only with customer approval).

2) Subprocessors: attached is our current roster (subprocessor_roster_v1.csv) filtered for subprocessors that could touch request payloads or logs. Short summary: three third parties — a metrics ingestion vendor in EU, an ops logging indexer in US, and a support-runbook vendor in APAC. All three are covered under our DPA and SCCs; we can provide SOC2 summaries and ATO artifacts on request.

3) KMS: For Private deployments, keys are customer-managed via BYOK and can be generated in the customer's region/KMS. For hosted mode, we offer region-scoped Redwood-managed keys; keys for each region are physically created in that region's KMS service and are only accessible to operations for emergency key rotation with logged JIT access. I'll attach a short diagram of the key flow.

4) Carve-out process: attached "regional-data-control-outline.pdf" describes our exception workflow: request -> risk review -> temporary approval window (max 48 hours unless extended) -> signed addendum if recurring. For pilots we typically allow a one-time temporary exception window with audit hooks and a required post-mortem.

Next steps: if acceptable, we'll prepare a one-page addendum for the pilot documenting the bounded-sync windows and the subprocessors list. If you need evidence packs (SOC2), Grace can run that. Happy to hop on a 30-min call Thursday.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: subprocessor_roster_v1.csv, regional-data-control-outline.pdf

Thanks Karthik — that helps. A couple of clarifying points from our DPO:

- For the analytics vendor in EU: does any request payload (PII) ever get forwarded to them, or is their dataset strictly aggregated/metric-level?
- For the APAC support vendor: we need confirmation they won't have access to raw prompt/response text except when a customer explicitly authorizes a session recording for triage. Can you confirm the default ACL?
- For the hosted KMS, can you confirm the audit log retention period and whether logs show the identity that performed a JIT key unwrap?

If you can reply in writing, we can avoid another round of paperwork. Also, for the short temporary exception windows: Acme will need the option to require a signed DocuSign acceptance form per exception (legal requirement).

On call availability: Thurs 11:00–14:00 PT works for us.

Subject: Re: Locality SLA exceptions and subprocessor roster — pilot questions

Mike — thanks for the follow-ups. I'm Grace, Redwood's privacy compliance lead; I'll own the evidence and addendum work for this pilot. Answers below and proposed formal steps.

- EU analytics vendor: we do not forward raw request payloads to that vendor. Their pipeline receives aggregated metrics and de-identified traces only (we strip prompt/response text prior to export). We can provide a sample export manifest and a hashed-only sample for review.

- APAC support vendor: default ACL is "no access" to raw prompt/response. Access is only granted via an explicit customer authorization flow that records the session id, approver, and purpose. We can add a clause to the addendum requiring that any access be logged with the session hash and customer approval.

- Hosted KMS audit logs: retention is 365 days by default for key unwrap events; logs include the Redwood operator identity (role-based) and machine principal. For Private deployments with customer-managed keys, Redwood never holds the plaintext key and cannot perform unwraps.

Process and commitments we propose for the pilot:
1) Redwood prepares a 1-page Addendum stating: allowed bounded sync windows (analytics up to 24h, debug traces up to 2h), subprocessors roster, KMS audit retention, and access controls for support vendor.
2) Each temporary exception requires: (a) a short rationale, (b) DPO sign-off or DocuSign approval, and (c) an automated post-event audit report within 48 hours.
3) We'll provide SOC2 summaries and a redacted evidence pack within 5 business days upon NDA.

If this aligns, Ben will generate the DocuSign addendum and the HubSpot deal will be updated to reflect the compliance milestone (ACME-4721). Proposed call Thurs 11:30 PT to finalize addendum language.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Privacy Compliance Lead
Redwood Inference
